headline.title: China’s AI models have Trump’s AI world at war with itself
headline.summary: Former advisors to President Trump have publicly criticized leading AI companies in the U.S., highlighting a growing divide in the AI landscape. The tensions reflect broader concerns about competition and regulatory approaches between American and Chinese AI models.

articles.title: X relaunches a rebuilt Android app after year-long effort
articles.summary: X has officially launched a rebuilt version of its Android app, which is now available globally after a year-long development effort. The updated app aims to enhance user experience and performance on the platform.

articles.title: OpenAI is scared of open-weight models. Should the US be?
articles.summary: The article discusses concerns surrounding the potential ban of Chinese-made open-weight large language models (LLMs) and the implications for AI commercialization. It highlights the challenges faced by companies like OpenAI in navigating the competitive landscape of AI while addressing security and regulatory issues.

articles.title: Introducing Cosmos 3 Edge
articles.summary: Cosmos 3 Edge has been launched as a new platform designed to enhance edge computing capabilities, enabling faster data processing and improved connectivity for IoT devices. The platform aims to streamline operations across various industries by integrating advanced AI technologies for real-time analytics and decision-making.

articles.title: Safety and alignment in an era of long-horizon models
articles.summary: OpenAI discusses the challenges and safety risks associated with deploying long-horizon AI models, emphasizing the importance of iterative deployment to identify failures and enhance safeguards. The article outlines key lessons learned to improve alignment and safety in AI systems.

articles.title: Adobe’s ‘natural look’ camera app embraces generative AI
articles.summary: Adobe's experimental camera app, Project Indigo, has been updated to include generative AI tools aimed at enhancing iPhone photography with a more natural look. Notably, the app's new features do not utilize Adobe's Firefly AI models.

articles.title: Adobe camera app’s new feature will critique your photos using AI
articles.summary: Adobe's Project Indigo has introduced a new feature in its camera app that utilizes AI to critique users' photos. Additionally, the app can now remove various backgrounds from images taken within the app.

articles.title: At SIGGRAPH, NVIDIA Advances Graphics and Simulation With Agentic and Physical AI
articles.summary: At SIGGRAPH, NVIDIA showcased advancements in graphics and simulation through the integration of agentic and physical AI technologies. These innovations are set to enhance media, content creation, and robotics by leveraging open models and real-time simulation capabilities.

articles.title: China delivers a one-two punch to America’s AI dominance
articles.summary: China's top AI firms, including Moonshot and Alibaba, have introduced competitive models that they assert can rival those from OpenAI and Anthropic, while being significantly more cost-effective. This development indicates a tightening race in AI technology, challenging America's current dominance in the field.

articles.title: YouTube clarifies policies around AI slop and upsetting videos
articles.summary: YouTube has revised its monetization policies to specify which types of AI-generated and low-quality videos are ineligible for ad revenue. The updates aim to provide clearer guidelines for content creators regarding acceptable video standards.

articles.title: AI is more likely than humans to form biases when hiring
articles.summary: A recent study indicates that AI systems are more prone to forming biases in hiring processes than humans, raising concerns about their fairness in evaluating job applicants. The research highlights that large language models (LLMs) not only inherit biases from their training data but can also develop their own biases independently.

articles.title: Bristol Myers Squibb Building Life Science Industry’s Most Advanced AI Factory on NVIDIA Vera Rubin
articles.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb has announced the deployment of its second NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD, enhancing its existing AI capabilities in the life sciences sector. The new AI factory, referred to as the "SuperDuperPOD," aims to further advance the company's research and development efforts.
